cards.prose: Matthew has the mountain *exceeding high* and the devil showing *all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them*. Luke has the same sight *in a moment of time*, and lets the devil say why he can offer it: *for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it* (Luke 4:6). In Luke the devil himself says the kingdoms have been put into his hand.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew's mountain is exceeding high and the devil shows all the kingdoms and their glory, which Luke has him say are delivered to him.

cards.prose: At Nazareth Yahusha (Jesus) says *unto none of them was Elijah sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon* (Luke 4:26), and that none was cleansed *saving Naaman the Syrian* (Luke 4:27). Beside *the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)*, they are sheep of that house who heard a prophet where it was scattered. The synagogue rose against him for saying the choosing is the Father's.
cards.member_sentence: The errand Matthew states is the one Luke has him name at Nazareth, with the widow of Sidon and Naaman as sheep who heard the prophet.
cards.flag: Old note's individual-mercy contrast reading dropped; written as the seed revealed in the lands of the scattering. Both Luke 4 Nazareth threads (title and summary) still carry the individual-mercy reading and need rewriting, so I joined the Matthew 15 thread instead.

cards.prose: Matthew says whom he was sent to: *the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)*. Luke shows what that errand looks like on the road. The town would have kept him, and he says he must preach in *other cities also*, *for therefore am I sent*. The sending moves him from city to city after those sheep.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew gives the boundary of his errand, the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), which is what Luke's therefore am I sent points to.
